statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). A ninth consecutive hour after the Globex reopen leaves the 28,981.00-29,100.00 band exactly unchanged, with NQ at 29,030.75 (-1.21%) having worked back to roughly the middle of that band from its lower third. WTI has eased further to 102.15, now nearer its 101.59 session low than its 103.58 high, and the Nikkei has recovered to -0.74% from a 62,726.18 low. Containment combined with genuine retracement in the index, in oil and in Japanese equities takes Tail one point below the watch band, while Stress stays high on the unresolved Saudi supply timeline and a near-certain Wednesday policy move.
recommendation: Tail sits one point below the watch band and well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The danger window is unchanged at 13:00-16:00 UTC, covering the 13:30 UTC US cash open and the first full cash hour, which together form the first US auction to price the weekend AI-pacing story, the Saudi East-West pipeline outage and an approximately 87% implied probability of a quarter-point policy move on Wednesday. The nearer checkpoint is the 07:00 UTC European cash open, where conditional Tail rises to 22. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold an unchanged 28,981-29,100 band for a ninth hour at -1.21% as NQ returns to mid-band, oil retraces toward its session low and Tokyo recovers
body:
A ninth consecutive hour of live price-path evidence leaves the structural read constructive and marginally better than the previous hour. NQ is quoted at 29,030.75, down 356.25 points or 1.21% against the 29,387.00 reference close, as of 02:16 EDT. The decisive structural fact is once more unchanged: the front-month day range is still exactly 28,981.00 to 29,100.00, the same 119-point band printed in the first hour after the Globex reopen. Nine hours without any range expansion, and without a chain of failed retracements, is the opposite of the price path that overwhelms a mean-reversion book. The incremental improvement this hour is location: NQ now sits near 42% of the band, back toward its middle, against roughly 29% an hour ago. A contract that drifts back into the centre of its range is demonstrating the retracement behaviour whose absence would define tail risk.

Cross-asset evidence has continued to soften in the same direction. WTI is 102.15, up 2.10%, having eased from 102.55 an hour earlier and now trading closer to its 101.59 session low than to the 103.58 high. Brent is 106.68, up 1.98%, against a 106.03 to 108.46 range, likewise nearer the low. The commodity that produced the original shock has given back a substantial part of the move inside the same session, which is retracement evidence rather than amplification. The Nikkei has extended its recovery to 63,535.28, down 0.74%, trading close to its 63,691.53 session high and well above the 62,726.18 low. Korea remains the negative outlier, with the KOSPI down roughly 2.6% at 6,732.00 and the semiconductor complex repricing hard, while Hong Kong is down about 0.4% and Australia is marginally positive. That dispersion is a sector de-rating, not a uniform index-level liquidation.

The macro backdrop is unchanged and firmly two-sided. Reuters reports that Goldman Sachs has reversed its call and now expects a 25 basis point increase at the 15-16 September FOMC meeting, with J.P. Morgan forecasting quarter-point moves in September and December, and market pricing at roughly 87% for a move this month against about 70% before the latest inflation data. Separately, Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline remains shut after drone damage, with industry sources indicating export stocks could be exhausted within five to seven days. Both are material to the distribution of outcomes into the middle of the week and are scored in Stress at 76, which eases one point as oil retraces. Neither is Tail evidence: the policy decision falls two days beyond the end of this forecast window, and an anticipated policy move is not a pathological price path.

Two evidence limits are stated plainly. The VIX at 15.84 and the 10-year at 4.975% are Friday cash closes rather than live prints, so the volatility and rates reads are stale by construction at this hour rather than absent; the H.15 release gives 4.56% on the 2-year and 4.95% on the 10-year for 10 September, up from 4.37% and 4.78% a week earlier. The shared cross-asset context file carried a partial collection status and a timestamp close to five hours old, so it was treated as stale and unusable, and the assessment rests entirely on independently fetched primary quotes and verified reporting. A secondary quote on the December contract showed -1.34% against the front month's -1.21%, a small divergence between delayed and current feeds that is noted rather than resolved. Confidence of 87 reflects that breadth of corroboration.

Conditional risk therefore stays concentrated in the 13:00-16:00 UTC stretch around the US cash open, peaking at Tail 24 in the first full cash hour, one point below the block band, rather than entering it on structure that has not been observed. The European cash open at 07:00 UTC is the nearer checkpoint, where conditional Tail rises to 22 as the first deep non-Asian pool to price the story. Beyond the 20:00 UTC US close, conditional Tail decays to 18 through the thin post-close and early Globex hours before rebuilding to 20 by the end of the window as Tuesday's European session and the Wednesday decision come into range.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours were available. Tail climbed steadily through the weekend from 8 at 06:00 UTC to 17 by 15:00 UTC, eased to 16, then stepped through 17, 18, 18 and 19 into the Globex reopen, crossing into the watch band at 21 and peaking at 22 in the reopen hour. Since the reopen it has been notably stable, printing 20 in seven of the last eight hours with a single 19 at 02:00 UTC. The mapped state was EA_ON and green for the first 15 hours, then WATCH and yellow for most of the reopen window with one EA_ON hour. Stress rose without interruption from 63 to 78 and has since settled in a 76-77 band as the pre-FOMC rates and energy backdrop accumulated. Confidence sat in the mid-80s through the weekend, dipped to the low 70s while live price-path evidence was unavailable during the Sunday halt, and has rebuilt to 87 as the Globex session produced continuous quotes. Dominant mode was normal for 17 hours, event/whipsaw in the reopen hour, and mixed for the last six.
outlookSummary: Conditional risk stays concentrated in the 13:00-16:00 UTC stretch around the 13:30 UTC US cash open, the first US auction to price the weekend AI-pacing story, the Saudi East-West outage and an approximately 87% implied probability of a Wednesday rate move together. The forecast peaks at Tail 24 in the first full cash hour, one point below the block band, rather than entering it on structure that has not been observed. The nearer checkpoint is the 07:00 UTC European cash open, where conditional Tail rises to 22 as the first deep non-Asian pool to price the story, and is held there through the first full European hour before easing. After the 20:00 UTC US close, conditional Tail decays to 18 through the thin post-close, Globex reopen and early Asian hours, which maps back to EA_ON, before rebuilding to 20 by the end of the window as Tuesday's European session and the Wednesday decision come into range. Confidence decays from 87 to 62 across the 24 slots, reflecting distance from observed evidence rather than any expected deterioration in the market.
